nodes.title: Bropilot Studio
nodes.description: A studio for collecting and visualising the knowledge graph of a system across its foundations, domain and implementation.

nodes.title: Shared understanding, codified
nodes.description: Capture the why, the what and the how of a system in one navigable graph so a team and its AI share a single source of truth.

nodes.title: Guided collection
nodes.description: Structured, kind-specific forms walk a user through every category of knowledge a system has, foundations through implementation.

nodes.title: Live graph view
nodes.description: Renders the whole system as an explorable, force-directed node-link graph that updates as the underlying data changes.

nodes.title: Portable spec
nodes.description: Imports and exports the canonical Bropilot JSON schema so a graph round-trips cleanly with external code generators.

nodes.title: Ontology-aware suggestions
nodes.description: Offers one-click edge suggestions and ranks search results by how well they fit the ontology, without ever forcing a choice.

nodes.title: Graph health linting
nodes.description: Surfaces advisory findings about orphaned nodes, missing why-chains, off-ontology edges and unverified surfaces.

nodes.title: Ontology-driven query
nodes.description: Runs schema-validated graph-pattern queries and derives named traversals like why-chains and evidence chains.

nodes.title: System architect
nodes.description: Owns the shape of the system and keeps the graph honest as it grows.

props.role: Designs and curates the knowledge graph

nodes.title: Builder
nodes.description: Turns the graph into running code, one module and component at a time.

nodes.title: Newcomer/onboarding engineer
nodes.description: Joins the project cold and needs the lay of the land fast, without reading every source file first.

props.role: Reads the graph to ramp up

nodes.title: The AI agent
nodes.description: Consumes and produces the same JSON graph as a human, extracting it from code or generating code from it.

nodes.title: Three-part model
nodes.description: Foundations, Domain and Implementation must each be first-class, navigable sections of the studio.

nodes.title: Code traceability
nodes.description: Every implementation node must link to where its code actually lives.

nodes.title: Round-trip with Bropilot skills
nodes.description: The exported JSON must import cleanly back through /bropilot-extract and /bropilot-generate with no lossy transform.

nodes.title: Advisory-only ontology
nodes.description: Ontology suggestions must never block or invalidate an edge a user actually wants to create.

nodes.title: Deterministic node ids
nodes.description: Every node id must be derivable from its kind and title alone, so imports and diffs stay stable.

nodes.title: Onboard onto a system
nodes.description: A newcomer reads the graph to understand a system fast instead of spelunking through source files.

props.situation: A new engineer joins and needs the lay of the land in an hour, not a week.

nodes.title: Explore via search
nodes.description: A user presses the search shortcut and jumps straight to any node by title, description or kind.

props.situation: Someone remembers a term but not which part of the graph it lives in.

nodes.title: Wire up a relationship
nodes.description: A user links two nodes together, guided by ontology suggestion chips instead of guessing at edge types.

props.situation: Two nodes clearly relate but no edge exists yet connecting them.

nodes.title: Copy context into an LLM chat
nodes.description: A user copies a token-budgeted markdown slice of a node's neighbourhood to paste into another conversation.

props.situation: Someone needs to hand an AI assistant just enough context about one part of the system.

nodes.title: Extract a graph from a codebase
nodes.description: An agent walks an existing repository and produces a Bropilot graph that models it.

props.situation: A team has code but no spec and wants one derived from what already exists.

nodes.title: No backend required
nodes.description: The studio runs entirely client-side, with no server component to deploy or keep alive.

props.invariant: The graph is always usable offline and stored entirely in the browser.

nodes.title: Single Vue island
nodes.description: The whole app is one Vue island so the editor and the graph can share live reactive state.

props.invariant: All interactive state lives inside one mounted island, never split across separate mounts.

nodes.title: SVG not canvas
nodes.description: The graph renders as SVG rather than canvas, trading raw performance for stylability and native hit-testing.

props.invariant: Every node and edge in the force graph must remain a real, hit-testable DOM element.

nodes.title: Nothing is ever validated or blocked
nodes.description: The ontology and lint layers only ever advise; they never refuse an edge or a node a user actually wants.

props.invariant: An off-ontology edge or unusual kind pairing must always be creatable, only ever flagged.

nodes.title: Faster alignment
nodes.description: Cut the time a team spends arguing about what the system actually is.

props.metric: Onboarding time and spec drift both trend down.

nodes.title: Zero drift between spec and code
nodes.description: Keep the knowledge graph and the running code close enough that either one can regenerate the other.

props.metric: Extracted graphs from the live repo match the hand-authored spec almost node for node.

nodes.title: Confident refactors
nodes.description: Let a builder change implementation details without fear of breaking an intent nobody wrote down.

props.metric: Fewer regressions traced back to an undocumented assumption.

nodes.title: Ship without re-litigating design
nodes.description: Keep past architectural decisions visible in the graph so teams stop re-debating settled questions.

props.metric: Design decisions referenced instead of re-argued in code review.

nodes.title: A graph beats a doc
nodes.description: A linked graph is retained and trusted better than an equivalent page of prose documentation.

props.belief: People reason about systems as connected things, not paragraphs.
props.validation: Users navigate edges more than they read descriptions in isolation.

nodes.title: Suggestions raise edge quality
nodes.description: Ranking targets and offering suggestion chips nudges users toward richer, more precise edge types.

props.belief: Most users pick the first sensible option rather than deliberate over edge types.
props.validation: Ontology-suggested edge types get chosen far more often than the weak, catch-all references type.

nodes.title: Seeded simulation catches invariant breaks
nodes.description: Replaying long sequences of randomly generated but schema-valid operations surfaces invariant violations that hand-written tests would miss.

props.belief: Random valid graph operations will eventually exercise an edge case manual tests miss.
props.validation: A failing seed reproduces the same operation sequence deterministically.

nodes.title: Users tolerate advisory noise
nodes.description: People will keep a few unresolved lint findings around rather than feel compelled to clear every one.

nodes.title: One island scales to hundreds of nodes
nodes.description: A single reactive Vue island can hold a few hundred nodes and edges without the UI becoming sluggish.

nodes.title: Contributors read CLAUDE.md before diving in
nodes.description: New contributors, human or AI, check the project's CLAUDE.md for prior decisions before re-proposing something already settled.

nodes.title: Space
nodes.description: One of four semantic groupings — basics, problem, solution or crosscutting — that drives node and edge colour.

nodes.title: Part
nodes.description: One of the three display groupings — Foundations, Domain or Implementation — that the studio navigates by.

nodes.title: Edge type
nodes.description: One of seventeen typed, directional relationships a graph edge can carry, grouped into five categories.

nodes.title: Why-chain
nodes.description: The traceable path of motivates, serves, implements and satisfies edges connecting a piece of code back to the intent that justifies it.

nodes.title: Ontology (T-Box)
nodes.description: The kind-to-kind triple table describing which edge types typically connect which kinds, layered advisory on top of the instance graph.

nodes.title: Triple strength
nodes.description: How strongly an ontology triple is endorsed — canonical, typical or merely possible — which drives dash-coding in the ontology view.

nodes.title: Node
nodes.description: A unit of knowledge with a kind, a title and a description, plus kind-specific fields kept in props.

nodes.title: Edge
nodes.description: A typed, directed relationship connecting a source node to a destination node.

nodes.title: Kind
nodes.description: One of the twenty-eight categories a node can belong to, each carrying its own display part, semantic space and editable fields.

nodes.title: Ontology triple
nodes.description: A single kind-to-kind-via-edge-type rule recorded in the T-Box, tagged with how strongly it is endorsed.

nodes.title: Finding
nodes.description: An advisory lint result pointing at a node or edge, describing an issue and never blocking anything.

nodes.title: Source reference
nodes.description: A quoted excerpt tying a node back to the interview answer or code passage that produced it.

nodes.title: Nodes connect via Edges
nodes.description: Edges link a source node to a destination node, and any node can carry many edges in either direction.

nodes.title: Kind maps to Part and Space
nodes.description: Every kind declares exactly one display part and one semantic space, and many kinds can share either.

nodes.title: Finding points at a Node
nodes.description: A lint finding optionally names the single node or edge it concerns, letting the UI navigate straight to it.

nodes.title: Ontology triple connects two Kinds
nodes.description: Each triple names a source kind and a destination kind, and the same pair of kinds can be linked by several different triples.

nodes.title: Autosave
nodes.description: Any change to the graph is persisted to localStorage immediately, debounced just enough to avoid thrashing storage.

nodes.title: Undo/redo history tracking
nodes.description: A debounced watch snapshots the graph after each pause in editing, so Cmd+Z and Cmd+Shift+Z step through real history points.

nodes.title: Off-ontology edge detection
nodes.description: Flags an edge whose kind pairing and type have no matching ontology triple, without ever refusing to save it.

nodes.title: Why-chain gap detection
nodes.description: Flags a capability, use case or goal that has no incoming motivates or serves edge explaining why it exists.

nodes.title: Orphan detection
nodes.description: Flags a node of a known kind that appears in no edge at all, in either direction.

nodes.title: Unverified surface detection
nodes.description: Flags a module, API or behaviour with no incoming verifies edge, so the health card always has something concrete to act on.

nodes.title: Node created
nodes.description: Fires whenever a new node is added to the graph, whether typed by hand or extracted from code.

nodes.title: Node selected
nodes.description: Fires when a user clicks a node in the graph or picks one from search, driving the Inspector panel.

nodes.title: Graph imported
nodes.description: Fires when a whole JSON graph replaces the current one via import or reset-to-sample.

nodes.title: Lint finding raised
nodes.description: Fires whenever the lint pass produces a new advisory finding against the current graph.

nodes.title: localStorage graph
nodes.description: The full { nodes, edges } JSON persisted under a single storage key, the sole source of truth on reload.

nodes.title: Undo/redo history stacks
nodes.description: Two bounded arrays of serialized graph snapshots, one for undo and one for redo, capped at fifty entries.

nodes.title: Selected node id
nodes.description: The id of the node currently shown in the Inspector, or null when nothing is selected.

nodes.title: Autosave timestamp
nodes.description: The moment of the most recent successful save, driving the small "Saved" indicator in the corner.

nodes.title: Collect a system
nodes.description: Walk the three parts in order, filling in what is known and leaving the rest for later.

nodes.title: Extract a graph from code
nodes.description: Mine an existing codebase's modules, components, tests and docs into a canonical Bropilot graph.

steps: Identify kinds per file and folder

nodes.title: Generate an SPA from a graph
nodes.description: Turn a Bropilot graph, in JSON, markdown or clipboard form, into scaffolded or updated application code.

nodes.title: Interview to build a graph
nodes.description: Build or extend a graph conversationally, patching the JSON file after every couple of answers rather than regenerating it.

steps: Load or start the graph file

nodes.title: Explore the graph via search
nodes.description: Open the search palette, type a fragment of a title or description, and jump straight to the matching node.

steps: Type a title, description or kind fragment

nodes.title: Studio
nodes.description: The single-page workspace shell hosting the sidebar navigation, every view and the Inspector panel.

nodes.title: Overview
nodes.description: The landing view summarising node and edge counts per part alongside the graph health card.

nodes.title: Graph
nodes.description: The full force-directed graph view, with an instance/ontology toggle and a search palette.

nodes.title: Foundations view
nodes.description: The part view listing every foundations-kind node with its guided editor form.

nodes.title: Domain view
nodes.description: The part view listing every domain-kind node with its guided editor form.

nodes.title: Implementation view
nodes.description: The part view listing every implementation-kind node with its guided editor form.

nodes.title: Graph store
nodes.description: Reactive graph state, autosave, undo/redo history and JSON import/export, all behind one small module.

nodes.title: Schema
nodes.description: The kind registry, the three parts, the four spaces, per-kind field defs and the edge-type ontology, all in one file.

nodes.title: Graph lint
nodes.description: Advisory graph-health checks against the ontology — never throws, never blocks, only ever suggests.

nodes.title: Graph query engine
nodes.description: A SPARQL-flavoured basic-graph-pattern kernel, JSON encoded, plus named traversals like why-chain and evidence.

nodes.title: Narrative generator
nodes.description: Composes one sentence per node from its description and its edges, turning a part into readable prose.

nodes.title: Router
nodes.description: Parses and builds the #/{view}/{nodeId} hash so navigation state lives in the URL.

nodes.title: Toast notifications
nodes.description: A tiny reactive queue of dismissable toast messages with optional actions.

nodes.title: Ontology simulator
nodes.description: A seeded, weighted operation generator that drives the real store through thousands of schema-valid mutations to hunt invariant breaks.

nodes.title: Suggestion engine
nodes.description: Derives ranked, advisory edge suggestions for a node from the ontology, favouring triangle-closing candidates.

nodes.title: ForceGraph
nodes.description: d3-force layout rendered as interactive, hand-rolled SVG — pan, zoom and drag without d3-zoom or d3-drag.

nodes.title: Studio
nodes.description: The root shell component: sidebar navigation, the active view, the Inspector panel and import/export controls.

nodes.title: Inspector
nodes.description: The side panel that shows a selected node's Details or generated Narrative, plus its lint badge.

nodes.title: RelationshipEditor
nodes.description: Lists a node's relationships and offers ontology suggestion chips for adding new ones.

nodes.title: NodeForm
nodes.description: A dynamic editor generated from a kind's field defs, so every kind gets a tailored form for free.

nodes.title: OverviewView
nodes.description: The landing screen: per-part counts, the graph health card and quick links into each part.

nodes.title: PartView
nodes.description: Lists every node of a given part with its NodeForm, parameterised by which of the three parts is active.

nodes.title: GraphView
nodes.description: Hosts ForceGraph plus the instance/ontology toggle, the search palette and the KindCard overlay.

nodes.title: KindCard
nodes.description: The bottom-right card shown in ontology mode listing a kind's live instances, with cross-layer jump-to-instance.

nodes.title: Graph
nodes.description: The serialisable shape of the whole knowledge graph: { nodes: GraphNode[]; edges: GraphEdge[] }.

props.signature: interface Graph { nodes: GraphNode[]; edges: GraphEdge[] }

nodes.title: GraphNode
nodes.description: The TS contract for a node: id, kind, title, description, and optional props and sourceRefs.

props.signature: interface GraphNode { id: string; kind: string; title: string; description: string; props?: Record<string, unknown>; sourceRefs?: SourceRef[] }

nodes.title: GraphEdge
nodes.description: The TS contract for an edge: id, srcId, dstId, type, and an optional label.

props.signature: interface GraphEdge { id: string; srcId: string; dstId: string; type: string; label?: string }

nodes.title: KindDef
nodes.description: The TS contract behind every entry in the KINDS registry: kind, label, part, space, icon and optional fields.

props.signature: interface KindDef { kind: string; label: string; part: Part; space: Space; icon: string; fields?: FieldDef[] }

nodes.title: localStorage Web API
nodes.description: The browser storage surface the graph store reads from and writes to on every change.

nodes.title: Clipboard API
nodes.description: The browser surface Copy Context writes markdown to, and the e2e suite reads back to assert on.

nodes.title: Hash-based routing API
nodes.description: The window.location.hash surface the Router reads and writes instead of a full client-side router.

nodes.title: Pointer Events API
nodes.description: The real pointerdown/mousemove/mouseup surface ForceGraph's hand-rolled pan, zoom and drag are built on.

nodes.title: Kebab-case id generation
nodes.description: Turns any title into the lowercase, hyphenated slug used to derive a fresh node id.

nodes.title: Basic graph pattern matching
nodes.description: Resolves a JSON-encoded match clause — inverse and transitive edges included — into a set of variable bindings.

nodes.title: Force-directed layout tick
nodes.description: Advances d3-force's simulation one step and bumps a frame counter so Vue's computeds re-read the mutated sim-node positions.

nodes.title: Ontology-valid operation generation
nodes.description: Generates a weighted, seeded sequence of schema-valid graph operations, reproducible from the same seed and op index.

nodes.title: bropilot repo
nodes.description: The single repository holding both Bropilot Studio and the three Bropilot skills.

nodes.title: d3-force
nodes.description: The physics simulation library driving ForceGraph's layout.

nodes.title: Vue
nodes.description: The reactive UI framework every component and the store are built on.

nodes.title: Astro
nodes.description: The static-site shell that mounts the single client:only Vue island.

nodes.title: Vitest
nodes.description: Runs the unit and seeded-simulator test suites.

nodes.title: Playwright
nodes.description: Drives the browser verification suite against a real Chromium instance.

nodes.title: nanoid
nodes.description: Generates short random suffixes for de-duplicated node and edge ids.

nodes.title: Tailwind v4
nodes.description: Utility CSS with no config file — theme tokens live in an @theme block in global.css instead.

nodes.title: GitHub Actions
nodes.description: Runs check, build, unit tests, e2e and the sync-skills drift gate on every push and pull request.

nodes.title: Schema unit tests
nodes.description: Exercises the KINDS registry, the ontology triple table and the kebab id helper.

nodes.title: Lint unit tests
nodes.description: Exercises every advisory lint rule: off-ontology edges, orphans, why-chain gaps and unverified surfaces.

nodes.title: Query unit tests
nodes.description: Exercises basic-graph-pattern matching plus the named why-chain, realization and evidence traversals.

nodes.title: Narrative unit tests
nodes.description: Exercises sentence generation from a node's description and its incoming and outgoing edges.

nodes.title: Suggestion unit tests
nodes.description: Exercises ranked, ontology-derived edge suggestions and their triangle-closing candidate ordering.

nodes.title: Ontology simulator tests
nodes.description: Replays seeded operation sequences against the real store and checks cheap and expensive invariants after each one.

nodes.title: Verification e2e suite
nodes.description: Codifies the full manual verification pass in Playwright, plus regressions caught by earlier fix batches.

nodes.title: CI pipeline
nodes.description: The GitHub Actions workflow that gatekeeps every push and pull request against main.

nodes.title: Graph health card
nodes.description: The Overview panel surfacing every current lint finding, each one clickable straight to its node.

nodes.title: Autosave status indicator
nodes.description: The small "Saved" ticker driven by the store's savedAt timestamp.

nodes.title: Glass dark theme
nodes.description: Translucent panels, per-space accent glows and refined typography across the whole studio.

nodes.title: Per-space accent hues
nodes.description: Each of the four semantic spaces gets its own accent colour, used consistently for node fills and legend chips.

nodes.title: Hand-rolled SVG interaction
nodes.description: Pan, zoom and drag built directly on pointer events instead of d3-zoom or d3-drag, chosen for finer control over hit-testing.
